legal_routes.name: Both-exit route: open both valves, send the sac, close CATCH after passage, then leave via the parcel gate

steps.goal: Open the upstream and receiver gates while preserving both heroes' routes.
steps.action: Move Isp to SEND and Pac to CATCH; maintain both holds while the boomerang carries the sac across the receiver gate.
steps.expected_feedback: Both cargo gates stay open and the light sac moves rightward with the outgoing boomerang.

evidence.claim: The two held pads open the two needed cargo-route gates.
The current exported-level replay records both authored holds active and later releases after the sac clears the receiver.

steps.goal: Let the sac clear the receiver before closing its valve.
steps.action: Step off CATCH only after the sac has passed the receiver gate; keep Isp at SEND until the sac is through the upstream gate.
steps.expected_feedback: Closing the receiver gate after passage leaves the cargo on the right for the return-to-PARCEL interaction.

evidence.claim: CATCH is a non-latching hold controlling the receiver gate.
The sampled successful route releases after the sac is at x642.5, past the receiver gate.

steps.goal: Use the returning projectile and PARCEL pad to open the exit gates.
steps.action: Allow the returning boomerang to finish its authored interaction; keep the heroes clear of the sac until it settles on PARCEL.
steps.expected_feedback: The sac activates PARCEL, which opens both exits; this is the cargo's return caught by the room's route geometry, not a hero reaching the pad.

evidence.claim: PARCEL accepts any weight and opens both exit gates; the return_stop is part of the current source.
The replay records the sac captured on PARCEL and both exit flags becoming true.

steps.goal: Reach each assigned exit after the cargo gate opens.
steps.action: Isp traverses the upper route and jumps to the Isp exit; Pac follows the lower route through the opened Pac exit gate to the Pac exit.
steps.expected_feedback: The level completes once both heroes overlap their own exits.

evidence.claim: Separate upper and lower static routes connect the two start regions to their exit approaches.
The current exported-level route completes with both exit flags true.
The replay is against current exported LEVELS and includes normal completion plus fall/re-entry and early/delayed release recovery cases.
The current source-exported, ordinary-input route completes in 6.233 simulated seconds; this is route feasibility evidence, not a human play observation.

isp: Occupies SEND to open the upstream gate while the boomerang sends the sac through.
Can leave SEND after the cargo has passed; then takes the upper route to the Isp exit once PARCEL opens both exits.
pac: Occupies CATCH to open the receiver gate while the sac travels across it.
Steps off CATCH after the sac clears the gate, enabling the return/receiver sequence, then takes the lower route to the Pac exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac steps off CATCH before the sac has cleared the receiver gate.
common_mistakes.consequence: The receiver gate closes while the sac is still approaching and stops its forward passage; the correct parcel-on-PARCEL exit state is delayed.
common_mistakes.recovery: Return Pac to CATCH to reopen the gate. If the projectile has already returned the sac to the left, maintain the holds and allow a later throw to carry it through, then release only after it clears. A sampled delayed retry completes without resetting; R remains available if a death requires a fresh room attempt.

evidence.claim: The early-release replay shows the receiver closing at sac x517.5, reopening at x594.5, and then a successful release after the sac clears.
The delayed retry waits 24 frames at the closed gate, reopens it, catches the return at x192, then sends the sac past x644 and completes both exits.
If recovery becomes impossible, R resets the attempt and increments retries.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac misses the lower route jump and falls off the shelf.
common_mistakes.consequence: Pac lands on the full-width safe catch floor rather than dying; the exit route is left behind.
common_mistakes.recovery: Jump back onto the lower route and continue. One sampled fall/re-entry route completed; arbitrary miss locations are not covered. If a later fall goes below the world, retry with R.

evidence.claim: The continuous catch floor spans the room and the room has no authored hazard rectangles.
A sampled fall reaches the bottom floor, then Pac re-enters the route and both exits complete.
R provides a full attempt retry if a fall becomes lethal.

reasoning.rationale: The route requires coordinating two held valves with a moving cargo object: keep both open through passage, release CATCH only after the sac clears, and let the return sequence activate PARCEL before exiting. That is a dependent plan with a non-obvious release point, beyond the first-pass estimate of one tentative causal choice.

evidence.claim: The two temporary route gates and crate-operated exit gate create the ordered dependency.
The successful replay demonstrates both holds, a release after passage, parcel capture, and later exit completion.

cooperation.rationale: Isp and Pac have distinct required pads and must hand off from maintaining those holds to separate exit routes. Their roles are not interchangeable because each valve accepts only its named hero. The first-pass estimate saw possible distinct roles but could not establish these requirements.

evidence.claim: Each valve accepts one specific hero and each hero has a separate required exit.
The legal ordinary-input route completes with both exit flags true.

execution.rationale: Source and route evidence show mostly flat travel on broad upper/lower surfaces with one short upper step and an optional lower route recovery. The main demand is the causal release sequence, not sustained precise platforming, so the first-pass estimate of several jump placements was high.

evidence.claim: Broad static floors provide the mandatory routes; the upper exit is one short rise above Isp's route.
A current source-exported route completes with ordinary input; route evidence is scripted feasibility, not a human performance measure.

timing.rationale: The sac must clear the receiver before Pac releases CATCH. This is one meaningful event-order/timing decision with a repeatable retry, rather than a narrow active window; the source replay shows a release after the sac reaches x642.5 and an early-release recovery.

evidence.claim: CATCH controls the receiver gate while the boomerang has an authored travel/return cycle.
The route release follows passage; an early release is recoverable by reopening CATCH.

hazards.rationale: The current mandatory route has no authored hazards, and the full-width catch floor makes a sampled Pac miss recoverable. The bright gaps seen in the idle image are not themselves lethal; only falling below the world is fatal, which the mandatory route does not require.

evidence.claim: A continuous catch floor is present and the authored hazard list is empty.
Falling becomes lethal only below the world boundary; ordinary floor contact does not kill.

novelty.rationale: The core boomerang-driven cargo action is already practiced in levels_35 and 31. What is new is its composition with hero-specific SEND and CATCH holds, release only after the sac clears, then the returning cargo landing on PARCEL to open both exit routes. This adds several linked pad and return relationships to a practiced cargo interaction, supporting novelty 3 without calling projectile cargo itself new.

evidence.claim: The frozen current-order snapshot places stable level_35 and level_31 before this room in the assessed campaign.

recovery_cost.rationale: A premature CATCH release delays the delivery and can require reopening the valve and waiting for another projectile cycle, but the current replay recovers without resetting and a missed Pac jump can use the safe floor. A death still costs a full room retry.

evidence.claim: Early-release retry completes after reopening CATCH.
A delayed closed-gate retry waits through another return/throw sequence and still completes without reset.
R restarts the whole room if a mistake becomes lethal.

solution_clarity.rationale: The visible SEND, CATCH, and PARCEL labels plus the contrasting one-way/return dialogue point toward the correct objects. They do not explain that Pac must release CATCH only after the cargo clears, or that the returning projectile is part of the gate-opening sequence. The hidden order remains a substantial clarity burden; the optional hint is not used to lower the unassisted score.

evidence.claim: The packet exposes the SEND/CATCH/Any Parcel labels and one-way-versus-returning text.
The three pad labels and route layout are visible, but the causal valve sequence is not shown in an activated state.
The optional hint contains the exact route/retry instruction; its presence does not establish that the base cues teach that sequence.

control_friction.rationale: The source assigns distinct key sets to Isp and Pac, but no shared-keyboard reliability or rollover test is in evidence. Logical bindings show no code-level key alias; physical control friction remains unmeasured.

evidence.claim: Isp and Pac have distinct movement and jump key mappings.

confidence_reason: Current authored source and a direct source-exported replay establish the cargo mechanism, a legal both-exit route, and two recovery cases. They do not establish browser/rendered behavior, discoverability, human success, or physical keyboard reliability. The reasoning and clarity burdens remain expert estimates.

confirmed: The separate starts, exits, SEND/CATCH labels, and returning-versus-one-way dialogue were visible as recorded.
The route does require Isp and Pac to contribute different held-pad roles; earlier movement, hold-pad, bridge, and return-attack cues exist at level_02, level_04, and level_07.
missed_mechanics: Cana's returning boomerang physically transports the light nutrient sac; the return/cargo route activates PARCEL, which opens both exits.
Pac must release CATCH after the sac clears its gate. Early release closes the gate; reactivation can recover the attempt, including after a delayed return/next-throw cycle.
A Pac miss can land on the safe bottom floor and re-enter the lower route in a sampled recovery.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rose from 2 to 3 because the actual objective is an ordered three-pad cargo sequence, not merely choosing between send and catch.
Cooperation rose from 2 to 3 because each valve accepts a different hero and both must hand off from the holds to separate exits.
Execution fell from 2 to 1 because the mandatory route uses broad static surfaces and little precision; the idle image made the gaps look more demanding than the route evidence supports.
Timing changed from unknown to 2 because one release must follow cargo passage, but the route has a recoverable repeat rather than a narrow window.
Hazards changed from unknown to 0 because the current source has no authored hazards and includes a continuous catch floor on the mandatory route.

Novelty remains 3 because the room recombines projectile-cargo transport already practiced in levels_35 and 31 with hero-specific SEND/CATCH holds, timed release, and a return-to-PARCEL gate sequence; projectile cargo itself is not new here.
Recovery cost changed from unknown to 2 because both an early-release retry and a sampled miss/re-entry route complete without a full reset.
Solution-clarity burden rose from 2 to 3 because the labels identify the objects but omit the critical release point and return/cargo dependency.
unresolved: Whether first-time players infer the release point from the visible base cues without opening the optional hint is not measured.
The source replay proves the authored route in simulation, not current rendered/browser acceptance or human performance.
The exact cost of other falls or an out-of-bounds death is not sampled; R retries the whole room.
Physical shared-keyboard reliability and one-person control interference remain unmeasured.

single_operator_note: One operator must alternate attention between Isp's SEND role and Pac's CATCH role, then move each hero to a different exit while observing the sac's position. The source replay demonstrates a two-input route only; it does not estimate one-person reliability or interference.
